metadata.title: ICCS 2016 User Guide for the International Database
metadata.venue: IEA International Civic and Citizenship Education Study 2016

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The ICCS 2016 International Database is designed for analyses that respect the study’s complex sampling design. The guide explains that sampling weights are needed to produce population-representative estimates and that analysts must select the appropriate weight variable for the specific analysis level (e.g., student-, school-, or teacher-level). It also provides variance estimation guidance using designated variance estimation variables, which are required for correct standard errors and confidence intervals under the complex design. The user guide does not present a single empirical analytic model; instead, it instructs users to apply the provided weight and variance estimation variables when computing statistics (e.g., regression, percentages, proficiency-level attainment) using the IEA IDB Analyzer.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a user guide for the ICCS 2016 International Database rather than an empirical study predicting an outcome from student-level data. As such, it does not implement an analysis pipeline that would require reporting a specific plausible-values (PV) strategy or a missing-data handling method for model estimation. The guide does include information on coding missing data and provides database resources, but it does not report an ML/achievement modeling results section where PV and missing-data procedures would be operationalized and evaluated.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used as a documentation guide for the ICCS 2016 International Database; no analytic subsample is defined in the provided text excerpt. The guide describes how to select appropriate records and variables (including weights and variance estimation variables) when users run their own analyses.

data.outcome_summary: This ICCS 2016 User Guide documents the ICCS 2016 International Database and how to analyze it correctly, rather than reporting empirical predictive results. It describes the database contents, including questionnaire data files, student civic knowledge test data files, within-country scoring reliability data files, and national contexts questionnaire data. The guide explains how to score civic knowledge test items (via SPSS or SAS syntax) and how to merge files across countries and across student, school, and teacher components using the IEA IDB Analyzer. It also provides detailed instructions for selecting sampling weights and variance estimation variables, emphasizing that analyses must account for the complex survey design. Finally, it outlines example analysis workflows (student-level analyses with/without civic knowledge scores, proficiency-level percentages, correlations, and analyses at teacher and school levels), including trend analysis options.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a technical user guide/data documentation for the ICCS 2016 International Database, not an empirical research paper with an ML target variable, model training, or reported performance metrics. Consequently, fields such as total_students, country-level sample sizes, PV handling, missing-data handling, and main_findings are not populated because the excerpt does not contain an implemented analysis with results. The guide’s purpose is to specify how analysts should use the provided weights, variance estimation variables, and scoring procedures when conducting their own analyses.
